question: My encrypted link between a Cisco router and a Linux router kept failing to come up properly. What did the fix involve changing on the Linux side?
answer: Changing the key-negotiation lifetime durations (IKE Phase 1 and Phase 2) on the Linux box.
support: We had to change the lifetime durations for IKE Phase1 & Phase 2 on the Linux Box

question: My PHP web service parses XML sent by browsers, and I'm worried the parser could be tricked into reading local files or probing internal hosts. Which PHP call mitigates this?
answer: libxml_disable_entity_loader(true);
support: In PHP you can help fix this by calling libxml_disable_entity_loader(true);

question: Two containers share a directory holding a local IPC socket file, but connecting gives a permission error even though file permissions look fine. What is the underlying cause?
answer: The containers are in different network namespaces, and UNIX domain sockets cannot be used between containers in different network namespaces.
support: Different containers cannot talk to each other via UNIX domain sockets when they are in different network namespaces.

question: In test-first development, what is the downside of writing a unit test that asserts a collaborator was called in a certain way, instead of checking the visible result?
answer: It makes the test more brittle since it depends on implementation details; worst case you must update the test when the implementation changes.
support: I do think that it makes your test more brittle

question: After upgrading my Linux desktop environment, opening a link from another app no longer switches me to the workspace where my browser window lives. Which window behavior setting restores that?
answer: Set focus stealing prevention to none, under systemsettings5 > Window Management > Window Behavior.
support: Change the Focus stealing prevention settings to none and your problem will be fixed

question: I granted a login the server-wide right to run bulk file loads, but it still can't load rows into my target database in SQL Server. What other permission does it need there?
answer: The INSERT permission, which is database/table-level; the server-wide bulk operations right alone is not enough to load into a database.
support: the user won't be able to BULK INSERT into a certain database if they don't have the INSERT permission as well

question: When automating build, deploy-to-dev and deploy-to-prod on my CI server, what rule of thumb decides where to split the work into separate jobs?
answer: Identify 'atomic' units: the smallest group of steps someone might need to run on their own, and make each its own job.
support: what are the smallest group of steps that you envision admins/ops/devs/etc. might need to run on their own

question: I forward web traffic through a router to an internal server, but once I apply an outbound filter on the router interface, external clients' HTTPS requests get no response. Why?
answer: The server's reply is sent to the client's random source port, which the outbound access-list doesn't permit, so the router drops it.
support: router wouldn't let the packet leave, because the destination port (that random port) is not specified in the access-list you have created.

question: When I trace the path across a wide-area network, some hops just show timeouts. Are those invisible switches sitting in the middle of the path?
answer: No. They are routers that do not send ICMP type 11 (TTL exceeded) replies.
support: they're hops (routers) that do not send ICMP type 11 packets to inform the TTL was exceeded

question: On a Windows web server, if I shut down a site while a page request is still running, does that in-flight request run to completion first?
answer: Yes. In a test with timed sleeps and a finally block, stopping the site mid-request still produced all six log entries.
support: the running process is finished before the site is shut down.

question: In my WPF app a base view model has one handler that picks the action from a string in the XAML. What problem arises if a child class must change just one action's behavior?
answer: You must copy the entire Execute(String parameter) method and change the one case statement, since you can't override a single command.
support: the only way to override behavior for one command is to copy the entire Execute(String parameter) method and change the one case statement

question: I have an executable script written in the classic Unix pattern-scanning language, and flags like -h are swallowed by the interpreter. With GNU coreutils 8.30 or newer, what shebang passes them through to the script?
answer: #! /usr/bin/env -S sh -c 'exec awk -f "$0" -- "$@"'
support: #! /usr/bin/env -S sh -c 'exec awk -f "$0" -- "$@"'

question: On SQL Server 2008 R2 or 2012, how can I quickly check whether my application relies on features slated for removal?
answer: Query sys.dm_os_performance_counters where object_name LIKE '%Deprecated%' and cntr_value > 0, ordered by cntr_value descending.
support: You can get a quick idea if your application is using any deprecated features by running

question: Why do many web API designers still put the release number in the endpoint path despite purists' objections?
answer: Because it's easy to implement and debug, and it makes clearly visible which version you are using.
support: the reason why many API designers do include an API version in the url is because it's easy to implement and debug

question: On a pair of Cisco Nexus switches sharing a multi-chassis port channel, must the trunk's allowed list of Layer 2 segments match on both switches to avoid the channel being suspended?
answer: No; the allowed VLAN list isn't a Type 1 or Type 2 consistency parameter, so a mismatch doesn't suspend the vPC.
support: You should be able to modify the allowed VLAN list without problems

question: I'm considering enabling Google's experimental faster web transport protocol on my TLS site. Which known attack on compressed headers and cookies is the security concern?
answer: The CRIME attack, which targets HTTP cookies; compressing encrypted data makes length depend on content, leaking information.
support: SPDY has been reported to be vulnerable to the CRIME attack

question: I want a clean record of every file a program's installer creates or alters on Linux so I can roll it back. Without special tooling, what is an easy approach?
answer: Boot a LiveUSB with a persistent data partition, snapshot the rw layer, then run the installer; all changes land on that overlay.
support: Possibly the easiest (?) way to do this is to boot off of a LiveUSB

question: Is there a standard name for a message-queue guarantee where messages sharing a key are handled one after another, while messages with different keys can run concurrently?
answer: 'Unit of Order' (UOO); e.g. Weblogic JMS lets you attach a UOO identifier so same-UOO messages are processed in chronological order.
support: Weblogic JMS will guarantee that messages of same UOO being processed in chronological order

question: With the standard stream editor and no extended-regex flag, how do I replace the final run of letters on each line of a file, ensuring it matches at least one letter?
answer: sed 's/[A-Za-z]\{1,\}$/replace/' file.txt
support: sed 's/[A-Za-z]\{1,\}$/replace/' file.txt

question: With SQL Server's built-in feature that captures row changes into history tables, is there one place to see which tables changed, or must I check each table?
answer: No central place; you must query each table individually using its fn_cdc_get_all_changes_dbo_tablename function.
support: The only way to do this is by querying each table individually
